title: California law sets fines for robotaxis that impede 911 response
key_facts: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 1246 'last week' (Mashable); a Senator Dave Cortese release is dated 30 Sep 2026 per search listings.
Under SB 1246, autonomous-vehicle operators such as Waymo and Tesla face hefty fines if their vehicles block first responders for more than 30 minutes; the article gives no amount.
The law also sets statewide standards for AV operators and emergency departments: two-way communication, company-hired local incident technicians for stalled vehicles, and updated fleet protocols.
More than 500,000 Waymo rides are completed every week; its fleet is more than 4,000 cars in 15 cities.
In July Representative Kevin Mullin introduced the House AV Emergency Response Coordination Act, citing robotaxis obstructing emergency vehicles in several cities.
A TechCrunch investigation found emergency responders were regularly asked to operate Waymo vehicles; NHTSA later urged makers to address a 'pattern' of interference.
